items.note: Would need the config's context/operationGuidance text as residue patterns over every artifact and the diff; that text is not available to cite, so no kind can express it here.

sources.quote: Do not copy `context` or `operationGuidance` verbatim into implementation files or planning artifacts unless the user separately asks for that content.

items.note: Comparing capability names against proposal headings needs a name-to-heading normalization (kebab vs Title Case) no selector offers; spotting task-like names needs judgment.

sources.quote: Do not name implementation tasks or proposal sections.

items.note: The document gives no list of catch-all names to use as a literal deny-list, so a cross_ref literal cannot be cited.
Every listed capability entry in New Capabilities uses kebab-case path segments (slash-separated). Fit with the existing spec organization is not checked.

sources.quote: Use kebab-case for path segments you introduce (e.g., user-auth or identity/user-auth) ... - `<capability-path>`: <brief description of what this capability covers>

items.note: Needs the Modified Capabilities names to be mapped to openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md at BASE_SHA; base_paths holds file paths, and no selector turns a capability name into that path.

sources.quote: Use the exact existing path under openspec/specs/.

items.note: .openspec.yaml is not a declared artifact, so its content cannot be checked under the condition that both capability sections are empty.

sources.quote: A change with no capabilities at all (pure refactor, tooling, docs) must set `skip_specs: true` in its .openspec.yaml - openspec validate rejects a zero-delta change without that marker.

items.note: The change artifact resolves only to changes/issue (or its archived -issue form), so its existence at the end of ff shows the fixed name was used.

unitemized.reason: This only lets the section be empty. Whether requirements change is a judgment call the run can't show, so no predicate can tie emptiness to it.
